text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Amsterdam Stock Exchange weighs the sale of its 60 pct stake in Kas-Associatie, bank specialising in providing securities services to market traders. (p1)
- Largest Dutch employers federation VNO-NCW diminishes its opposition to equal employment act for ethnic minority workers, after minister's statement to soften the legislation. (p1)
- Amsterdam's agricultural futures market ATA in talks to become part of Amsterdam Options Exchange EOE-Optiebeurs. (p1)
- Steelmaker Hoogovens' path eased to set up a joint-venture with Belgian Usines Gustave Boel (UGB). (p1) - Food company Verkade to shed 79 jobs in restructuring its Zaandam-based plant. (p3)
- KPN subsidiary, cable company Casema, angered about Arnhem's decision to go over to rival company Telekabel. (p3)
- Food and detergent group Unilever possibly in white knight role in Germany's detergent company Henkel's takeover attempt of U.S. Loctite. (p5)
- New technologies force Dutch publishers to reconsider their position. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- French president Jacques Chirac blocks French-Dutch drugs agreement; Dutch government hopes for Germany's support. (p1)
- Tyre producer Pirelli Tyre Holding possibly disappears from Amsterdam Stock Echange. (p2)
- Rich Rotterdam family De Monchy, helped by investor Michael Cook and raider Henk van den Hombergh, hunts for power over AIR Holding. (p2)
- Publisher PCM takes over Dutch press databank NPD from automation company Roccade. (p31)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Parliament takes first step towards giving homosexual partnership registration same legal rights as marriages. (p1)
- Insurer Delta Llyod expects an end to the ongoing mortgate rate decreases. (p1)
- Number of foreign tourists visiting the Netherlands drops four percent. (p9)
- Participation group Alpinvest, Candover Partners and Electra Fleming take over some 75 pct of shares in British companies.
TROUW
- Older Dutch diplomats abroad take public stands opposed to official Dutch drugs policy, say researchers of Amsterdam University to the French press. (p1)
- Sport-only commercial TV Sport7 is looking for new partner in an attempt not to lose Philips as shareholder.(p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Chemicals concern Akzo Nobel passes over the Netherlands for its new Dfl 225 million fibre plant. (p10)
- Steel association firm Grootint shutters its Dordrecht plant. (p11)
